message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.21","text":"When he had said these things, I answered, “Already I give thanks to God, for just as I wished to be fully assured, so he has also granted it to me. Nevertheless, be so unconcerned about matters concerning me that I will never at any time doubt—to such a degree that, even if you yourself should ever wish to move me away from the prophetic thesis, being powerless you would not be able to do so. So well do I know what I have received. And certainly do not think that I am promising you something great in this very claim that I will never doubt. Rather, neither I myself nor any other human being who has heard the discourse concerning a prophet will ever be able to doubt the true thesis, once he has first heard and understood what the truth of prophetic proclamation is. Therefore, be confident in the teaching willed by God, for every craft of evil has been defeated. Against prophecy nothing has any power: neither verbal arts nor contrivances of sophisms, neither syllogisms nor any other device—provided, at least, that the one who has listened to a true prophet genuinely desires truth and is not, under the pretext of truth, looking around for something else. So, my lord Peter, do not lose heart as though you had bestowed the greatest good on someone without perception. For you bestowed it on one who perceives the favor and cannot be led astray from the truth that was given. For I know that there are things a person wants both to receive quickly and not to obtain slowly. I therefore know not to despise, because of its speed, what was given to me, incomparable and alone secure.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς γὰρ ἐβουλόμην πληροφορηθῆναι","chosen":"for just as I wished to be fully assured","rationale":"The passive πληροφορηθῆναι denotes attaining full assurance rather than merely receiving information."},{"source_quote":"τῆς προφητικῆς ὑποθέσεως","chosen":"the prophetic thesis","rationale":"Ὑπόθεσις denotes the position or foundational proposition concerning prophecy; “subject” remains possible but is less precise here."},{"source_quote":"ἀδυνατῶν οὐ δυνήσῃ","chosen":"being powerless you would not be able","rationale":"The rendering preserves the source’s emphatic repetition of the same verbal root."},{"source_quote":"προφητικῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἀλήθεια","chosen":"the truth of prophetic proclamation","rationale":"In this context ἐπαγγελία can denote a declaration or profession; “prophetic promise” remains a possible alternative."},{"source_quote":"τῷ θεοβουλήτῳ δόγματι","chosen":"in the teaching willed by God","rationale":"The rendering expresses the compound θεοβούλητος and takes δόγμα as an authoritative teaching."},{"source_quote":"πᾶσα γὰρ τέχνη κακίας νενίκηται","chosen":"for every craft of evil has been defeated","rationale":"Τέχνη retains the sense of practiced art or craft, while the perfect passive marks its defeat as accomplished."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε τέχναι λόγων οὔτε σοφισμάτων ἐπίνοιαι, οὐ συλλογισμοί, οὐκ ἄλλη τις μηχανή","chosen":"neither verbal arts nor contrivances of sophisms, neither syllogisms nor any other device","rationale":"The ordered list of rhetorical arts, devised sophisms, formal arguments, and other mechanisms is preserved."},{"source_quote":"οὐ προφάσει ἀληθείας ἕτερόν τι περιβλέπεται","chosen":"is not, under the pretext of truth, looking around for something else","rationale":"Περιβλέπεται preserves the image of looking around for another objective while using truth as a pretext."},{"source_quote":"ἀπατηθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δοθέντος ἀληθοῦς","chosen":"be led astray from the truth that was given","rationale":"The neuter substantive ἀληθές is understood as “truth,” though “the true thing given” is grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι ἔνεστιν ὧν βούλεταί τις καὶ ταχέως λαβεῖν καὶ βραδέως μὴ τυχεῖν","chosen":"For I know that there are things a person wants both to receive quickly and not to obtain slowly","rationale":"Βούλεται governs both infinitival expressions, preserving the pointed contrast between quick and delayed acquisition."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τὸ τάχος ἀσυγκρίτου καὶ μόνου ἀσφαλοῦς","chosen":"because of its speed, what was given to me, incomparable and alone secure","rationale":"Διὰ τὸ τάχος gives the possible ground for despising the gift, while the genitive adjectives characterize what was given."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.22","text":"After I had said these things, Peter said, “I acknowledge my gratitude to God both for your salvation and for my own enjoyment. For I truly rejoice, knowing that you have recognized just what the greatness of prophecy is. Since, then, as you said, even if I myself should ever wish—may that be far away!—to move you over to another teaching, I would not be able to persuade you, begin from tomorrow onward to be present with me at the debates with the opponents. Tomorrow I am to face Simon the magician.” And after saying this and himself partaking privately of food, he instructed me also to partake. Then, after blessing over the food and giving thanks, after he had eaten his fill and had also given me the reason for this very thing, he added, saying, “May God grant you to become like me in every respect and, after being baptized, to share the same table with me.” After saying these things, he instructed me to rest, for by then, I suppose, the nature of the body was also demanding sleep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Χάριν ὁμολογῶ τῷ θεῷ","chosen":"I acknowledge my gratitude to God","rationale":"Ὁμολογῶ gives the gratitude the force of an expressed acknowledgment."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς ἐμῆς ἀπολαύσεως","chosen":"for my own enjoyment","rationale":"Ἀπόλαυσις denotes Peter’s own enjoyment or delight arising from Clement’s response."},{"source_quote":"τί ποτ’ ἐστὶν προφητείας μέγεθος","chosen":"just what the greatness of prophecy is","rationale":"Ποτέ in this interrogative expression adds emphasis represented by “just what.”"},{"source_quote":"ὅπερ ἀπείη","chosen":"may that be far away!","rationale":"The optative expresses a strong wish that the contemplated action remain far removed."},{"source_quote":"ἄρξαι τοῦ λοιποῦ ἀπὸ τῆς αὔριον παρεῖναί μοι","chosen":"begin from tomorrow onward to be present with me","rationale":"“From tomorrow onward” represents both ἀπὸ τῆς αὔριον and the prospective force of τοῦ λοιποῦ."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ταῖς τῶν ἀντικειμένων ζητήσεσιν","chosen":"at the debates with the opponents","rationale":"Ζητήσεις denotes adversarial discussions here, while the genitive identifies those taking the opposing side."},{"source_quote":"ἔστι δέ μοι ἡ αὔριον πρὸς Σίμωνα μάγον","chosen":"Tomorrow I am to face Simon the magician","rationale":"The idiomatic rendering preserves the prospective sense and the adversarial force of πρός; μάγον is treated as a description."},{"source_quote":"τροφῆς αὐτὸς μεταλαβὼν ἰδία κἀμὲ μεταλαβεῖν ἐκέλευσεν","chosen":"himself partaking privately of food, he instructed me also to partake","rationale":"The translation provisionally treats ἰδία as the intended adverb and attaches it to Peter’s partaking; its form and placement remain uncertain."},{"source_quote":"εὐλογήσας δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς τροφῆς καὶ εὐχαριστήσας","chosen":"after blessing over the food and giving thanks","rationale":"The two distinct acts, blessing and giving thanks, are both retained."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοῦ τούτου τὸν λόγον μοι ἀποδοὺς","chosen":"having also given me the reason for this very thing","rationale":"Τὸν λόγον ἀποδιδόναι here most naturally means supplying the reason or explanation for the action just described."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ πάντα ἐξομοιωθῆναί μοι","chosen":"to become like me in every respect","rationale":"The passive ἐξομοιωθῆναι expresses being brought into likeness, with κατὰ πάντα specifying every respect."},{"source_quote":"βαπτισθέντα τῆς αὐτῆς μοι μεταλαβεῖν τραπέζης","chosen":"after being baptized, to share the same table with me","rationale":"The participle presents baptism as antecedent to participation, while μεταλαβεῖν with the genitive is rendered “share.”"},{"source_quote":"ἤδη γάρ που καὶ τὸν ὕπνον ἀπῄτει ἡ τοῦ σώματος φύσις","chosen":"for by then, I suppose, the nature of the body was also demanding sleep","rationale":"The enclitic που gives the statement a mildly tentative or inferential force."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τροφῆς αὐτὸς μεταλαβὼν ἰδία κἀμὲ μεταλαβεῖν ἐκέλευσεν","issue":"The supplied and image-checked print reads “ἰδία,” which is difficult in the apparent adverbial syntax. The expected adverbial form would be “ἰδίᾳ.” Even with that conjecture, the word’s placement leaves unresolved whether “privately” modifies Peter’s partaking or Clement’s commanded partaking.","proposed_reading":"τροφῆς αὐτὸς μεταλαβὼν ἰδίᾳ κἀμὲ μεταλαβεῖν ἐκέλευσεν","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
